We propose VI sual G eneralization via latent-space c O nsistency in model-based R L ( VIGOR ), a framework that enables zero-shot generalization while retaining the sample efficiency of its TD-MPC2 backbone. VIGOR addresses the two-level vulnerability through three interdependent components: (i) asymmetric weak-to-strong augmentation (AW), an asymmetric batch-splitting strategy that produces paired weak-only and weak-to-strong latents; (ii) dynamics-level consistency (DC), which enforces augmentation-invariant transition predictions by anchoring dynamics outputs to stable targets; and (iii) encoder-level stabilization (ES), which prevents the shared encoder from drifting under the cross-augmentation pressure imposed by DC. We evaluate VIGOR on the DeepMind Control Suite (DMC) [ 40 ] and Robosuite [ 54 ] under the RL-ViGen zero-shot protocol [ 49 ] , covering seven visual distraction types—a substantially broader evaluation than the two types ( background-color , background-video ) typically considered in prior work [ 18 , 20 , 4 , 7 ] (Appendix D.3 ). VIGOR outperforms state-of-the-art MFRL and MBRL baselines, improving zero-shot generalization over the second-best baseline by 3.4 % 3.4\% on DMC and 43.6 % 43.6\% on Robosuite while retaining the sample efficiency of its TD-MPC2 backbone. Ablation studies further reveal that naive transfer of MFRL strategies fails in MBRL: applying strong augmentation uniformly across the batch, without the asymmetric splitting of AW, achieves only 48 % 48\% of VIGOR’s performance on DMC (Section 4.3 ). Furthermore, VIGOR’s robustness is augmentation-agnostic: latent-space consistency, rather than any specific augmentation choice, drives generalization (Section 4.4 ; Appendix E.5 ). Our contributions are: • Problem identification and analysis. We identify a two-level failure mode in MBRL: visual distractions first produce OOD encoder outputs, which then compound through recursive rollouts—a failure mode unique to recursive latent dynamics (Figure 1 ; Section 4.5 ). • Integrated framework for MBRL robustness. We propose VIGOR, which addresses this failure mode through three interdependent components (AW, DC, and ES) designed for the recursive world-model setting. We show that naive transfer of MFRL strategies fails in MBRL, that VIGOR’s integration is necessary, and that the resulting robustness is augmentation-agnostic (Sections 4.3 – 4.5 ; Appendix E.5 ). • State-of-the-art zero-shot generalization. VIGOR outperforms MFRL and MBRL baselines, surpassing the second-best baseline by 3.4 % 3.4\% on DMC and 43.6 % 43.6\% on Robosuite while preserving the strong sample efficiency of its TD-MPC2 backbone. 2 Related Work 2.1 Visual Model-Based Reinforcement Learning Latent-space MBRL learns compact world models for planning or imagination in latent space [ 6 , 10 , 12 , 14 , 17 ] . The Dreamer series adopts a decoder-based architecture that reconstructs pixel observations [ 9 , 11 , 12 ] , whereas TD-MPC uses a decoder-free architecture that plans without reconstruction [ 14 , 17 ] . Both families assume i.i.d. training and test distributions; in practice, unseen visual distractions push encoder outputs out of distribution, causing compounding rollout errors (Figure 1 ). VIGOR equips latent-space MBRL with three interdependent components (AW, DC, and ES) designed to mitigate this failure mode. An extended discussion of MBRL architectures and our backbone selection rationale is provided in Appendix F . 2.2 Visual Generalization in Model-Free Reinforcement Learning MFRL approaches address visual robustness through data augmentation [ 16 , 20 , 37 ] , self-supervised representation learning [ 18 , 4 ] , and pretrained visual encoders [ 48 , 32 ] . These methods operate at the single-step level: the encoder maps observations directly to Q-values or policy outputs without recursive rollouts. In MBRL, by contrast, encoder perturbations propagate through multi-step latent rollouts and compound across the planning horizon, motivating VIGOR’s two-level design. A detailed survey is provided in Appendix G.1 . 2.3 Visual Generalization in Model-Based Reinforcement Learning Invariant MBRL methods [ 50 , 41 , 53 , 39 , 52 ] learn representations that discard task-irrelevant visual factors but typically require test-time adaptation . VIGOR targets the stricter zero-shot setting where no adaptation data are available. Dr. G [ 7 ] is the most directly comparable prior work, as it explicitly targets zero-shot generalization in latent-space MBRL. It extends Dreamer [ 9 ] with dual contrastive objectives and an inverse-dynamics auxiliary loss. VIGOR differs in mechanism: rather than contrastive negatives and auxiliary supervision, it enforces dynamics-level consistency (DC) through direct latent regression, supported by asymmetric weak-to-strong augmentation (AW) and encoder-level stabilization (ES). Built on TD-MPC2 [ 17 ] , VIGOR targets the same zero-shot setting through a fundamentally different inductive bias. A detailed survey is provided in Appendix G.2 . 3 VIGOR VIGOR addresses the two-level vulnerability identified in Section 1 : visual distractions first perturb encoder outputs, and these perturbations then compound through recursive latent rollouts. The framework comprises three interdependent components, each targeting a different level of the world-model pipeline: input augmentation, latent dynamics, and encoder representation. Figure 2 provides an overview. The three components depend on each other: AW produces the paired latents on which DC operates; DC stabilizes dynamics but can cause encoder drift; ES counteracts this drift. Because AW modifies only the input pipeline while DC and ES act through auxiliary losses, VIGOR can be integrated into latent-space MBRL frameworks without modifying the underlying planner or optimization procedure. 3.1 Asymmetric Weak-to-Strong Augmentation (AW) We distinguish between weak augmentations (minor perturbations that preserve most visual information) and strong augmentations that impose substantial visual changes. Additional visualizations are provided in Appendix E.8 ; we further verify that this consistency holds under deeper planning horizons up to H = 10 H{=}10 (Appendix E.9 ). 5 Conclusion We introduced VIGOR , a framework that achieves robust zero-shot visual generalization in latent-space MBRL while preserving the strong sample efficiency of its TD-MPC2 backbone. VIGOR addresses the two-level vulnerability of latent-space MBRL: visual distractions perturb encoder outputs, and these perturbations compound through recursive rollouts. The framework integrates three interdependent components (AW, DC, and ES) to mitigate this failure mode. Across challenging OOD benchmarks, VIGOR surpasses the second-best baseline by 3.4 % 3.4\% on DMC and 43.6 % 43.6\% on Robosuite. Ablation studies confirm that all three components are jointly necessary and that VIGOR’s robustness is augmentation-agnostic: latent-space consistency, not any particular augmentation choice, is what drives generalization. Limitations and future work. VIGOR targets appearance-based perturbations and does not address geometric distortions; evaluations under unseen camera rotations (Appendix E.10 ) reveal that such shifts remain challenging, motivating geometry-aware representations as a primary future direction. Beyond visual shifts, extending VIGOR to dynamics- and task-level shifts [ 36 , 5 ] is a natural next step, and validating it in real-robot deployments would assess its practical applicability.
